(b) Suggest why the measured pH of the chloroethanoic acid solution is slightly higher than calculated. (c) Describe a chemical test, other than pH, to show that both are carboxylic acids.
items.answer: (a) Cl withdraws electron density (negative inductive effect), delocalising the negative charge and stabilising the chloroethanoate ion. items.stem: Explain why chloroethanoic acid is a stronger acid than ethanoic acid.

items.stem: Explain why propanoic acid is slightly weaker than ethanoic acid.

pKa values: benzoic acid 4.2; ethanoic acid 4.76; chloroethanoic acid 2.86. Arrange the acids in order of increasing strength and explain the position of the strongest acid.
items.answer: ethanoic acid < benzoic acid < chloroethanoic acid; strongest: chloroethanoic acid, because electron-withdrawing halogen atoms stabilise the carboxylate ion.

items.stem: Ravi measures the pH of 0.2 mol dm⁻³ solutions of ethanoic acid (pKa 4.76) and chloroethanoic acid (pKa 2.86) in a school laboratory. (a) Calculate the expected pH of each solution. (b) Suggest why the measured pH of the chloroethanoic acid solution is slightly higher than calculated.
items.answer: (a) ethanoic 2.73; chloroethanoic 1.78 (b) The approximation [HA] ≈ initial concentration is less valid for a stronger weak acid, as a significant fraction dissociates.

items.stem: Lucas converts propanoic acid into propanoyl chloride and then uses it to make three derivatives. (a) Describe what is seen when the acyl chloride is added to water and write an equation. (b) Explain why acyl chlorides are more reactive towards nucleophiles than carboxylic acids.
items.answer: (a) Vigorous reaction, steamy white fumes of HCl; CH₃CH₂COCl + H₂O → CH₃CH₂COOH + HCl (b) Cl is more electron-withdrawing and a better leaving group; the carbonyl carbon is more δ+, and Cl⁻ is lost easily in the elimination step.

items.stem: Tomás converts ethanoic acid into ethanoyl chloride and then uses it to make three derivatives. (a) Give a reagent for converting ethanoic acid into ethanoyl chloride and write the equation. (b) Explain why acyl chlorides are more reactive towards nucleophiles than carboxylic acids. (c) Explain why the reaction with phenol is used to make the phenyl ester.
items.answer: (a) SOCl₂: CH₃COOH + SOCl₂ → CH₃COCl + SO₂ + HCl (or PCl₅ / PCl₃ with heat) (b) Cl is more electron-withdrawing and a better leaving group; the carbonyl carbon is more δ+, and Cl⁻ is lost easily in the elimination step. (c) Phenol reacts only very slowly with carboxylic acids, because its lone pair is delocalised into the ring (poor nucleophile).

items.stem: Which is the correct definition of the term "leaving group"?
options: An atom or group, such as Cl⁻, that departs with the bonding pair of electrons during the elimination step.
The δ+ carbon atom of a C=O group, attacked by nucleophiles.
A species with a lone pair of electrons that it donates to an electron-deficient atom to form a new bond.
A symbol showing the movement of a pair of electrons from a lone pair or bond to an atom or new bond.
items.answer: An atom or group, such as Cl⁻, that departs with the bonding pair of electrons during the elimination step.

items.stem: A student in Nairobi states: "In the addition–elimination mechanism, Cl⁻ leaves first to form a carbocation." Explain why this statement is incorrect.
items.answer: The nucleophile adds first to the carbonyl carbon; Cl⁻ leaves when the C=O bond reforms.

items.stem: Tariq studies the reaction of ethanoyl chloride, CH₃COCl, with methanol, CH₃OH, at room temperature. (a) Describe the mechanism, showing curly arrows in words, and draw-describe the intermediate. (b) Name the organic product and give its structural formula.

items.stem: The pKa of bromoethanoic acid, CH₂BrCOOH, is 2.9. Calculate the pH of a 1 mol dm⁻³ solution of the acid.

Grace measures the pH of 0.2 mol dm⁻³ solutions of ethanoic acid (pKa 4.76) and chloroethanoic acid (pKa 2.86) in a university teaching laboratory. (a) Explain why chloroethanoic acid is the stronger acid. (b) Predict, with a reason, the pKa of dichloroethanoic acid relative to the two acids.
